```{R, echo=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
```

```{R, echo=FALSE}
# prettify dataset
library(stringr)
mtcars$brand <- word(rownames(mtcars), 1)
#mtcars$brand <- sapply(rownames(mtcars), function(x){ x[, 6]})
mtcars$cyl <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)
```

# Some example datasets

In this workshop, we'll be using two common example datasets to illustrate data visualizations: the `mtcars` and `diamonds` datasets.
Both are supplied by any standard installation of the R language.

The mtcars dataset is a common small example dataset used for illustrating different plots.
It contains the technical specifications of different car models by various manufacturers.
Some lines of the dataset are given below, as it may be helpful to understanding some of the plots below.

```{R}
mtcars[1:10,]
```

The diamonds dataset is another common example dataset. It is much bigger than the mtcars dataset.
It contains data on the properties and auction price of many diamonds.
Some rows are again

```{R}
diamonds[1:10,]
```

# Finding the components of a plot

Grab a partner, and take a look at the following plots, produced from a common example dataset containing the technical specifications of different car models.
List the visual primitives each plot is composed of, and which variables of the dataset are displayed in the plot.
Investigate which messages they communicate to a reader.

## `mtcars` plots

```{R, echo=FALSE}
# format as gggrid?
grid.arrange(
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_point(aes(x=wt, y=mpg)),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_line(aes(x=wt, y=mpg)),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_bar(aes(x=1, fill=cyl)),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_point(aes(x=hp, y=disp, shape=cyl))
#	ggplot(mtcars) +
#		geom_bar(aes(gear)) +
#		coord_polar(theta="x")
#	ggplot(mtcars) +
#		geom_rug(aes(x=wt, col=mpg))
#	ggplot(mtcars) +
#		geom_point(aes(x=wt, y=(4.54/161)/mpg)) +
#		ylab("l/100km")
	)
```

## `diamonds` plots

```{R, echo=FALSE}
# format as gggrid?
grid.arrange(
	ggplot(diamonds) +
		geom_bar(aes(x = 1, fill=clarity), width=1) +
		coord_polar(theta="y"),
	ggplot(diamonds) +
		geom_bar(aes(x = 1, fill=clarity), width=1) +
		coord_polar(theta="x"),
	ggplot(diamonds) +
		geom_bar(aes(x=clarity, fill=clarity), width=1) +
		coord_polar(theta="x"),
	ggplot(diamonds) +
		geom_violin(aes(price, x = clarity)) + 
		scale_y_log10()
)
```

# Statistics in plotting

Have a look at the plots below with your partner.
Which statistics are computed from the dataset to make the plot, and which graphical components do they correspond to?
Does this assignment make sense?

```{R, echo=FALSE}
grid.arrange(
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_histogram(aes(wt), binwidth=0.5),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_violin(aes(hp, x=cyl)),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_boxplot(aes(cyl, wt)) +
		geom_point(aes(x=cyl, y=wt)),#, col=mpg)),#, shape=brand)),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_smooth(aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) +
		geom_point(aes(x=wt, y=mpg)),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_text(aes(x=hp, y=qsec, label=brand), check_overlap=TRUE),
		#geom_text(aes(x=hp, y=cyl, label=brand), check_overlap=TRUE),
	ggplot(mtcars) +
		geom_smooth(aes(x=hp, y=disp), method='lm') +
		geom_point(aes(x=hp, y=disp, col=cyl)) +
		coord_polar(theta="x")
		)
```

# Napoleons plot in the grammar of graphics

Below is reproduced a famous 19th century plot of Napoleons 1812-13 winter campaign by Charles Minard.
This plot was originally drawn by hand and reproduced by lithography; nonetheless, it can be described using the grammar of graphics.


![Plot of napoleons troop movement in the winter of 1812-13.](./napoleongraphic.png){width=50%, height=50%}
